summary: Cells that form from randomly scattered catalysts persist as individuals (L2), including two-sector 'Janus' cells from t~180. A looser mutant kind spreads inside them, against a neutral control on 3 seeds.

claims.statement: Cells that form from randomly scattered catalysts persist as individuals (L2), including two-sector 'Janus' cells from t~180. A looser mutant kind spreads inside them, against a neutral control on 3 seeds.
claims.spontaneity_basis: init() scatters N=4000 particles uniformly at random and makes ~0.5% of them (about 20) catalyst cores (frac_C=0.005) at random; no bodies or templates are planted. seed_kind1=0, so the second kind arises only by mutation. The cells form from the random catalyst scatter, as in sporecell. Per the coordinator's S ruling this is a random particle soup over the whole box (every particle's position and type drawn i.i.d.; the ~20 catalysts are single particles inside that soup, not placed clusters), so S stands.
claims.caveats: L6[L2] Weak: the 'gen 9' lineage is a ratchet staircase of individuals that live 10-60 t. The selection evidence is at mu=0.01, while the pack runs at mu=0.002. The world runs on the same unconverged dt=0.02 integrator as sporecell and was not rerun step-safe.
